finding.claim: Address6.parse() builds AddressError.parseMessage by wrapping the offending characters in a span without HTML-escaping them. The documented contract (src/address-error.ts:8-12) says the content is escaped and safe to insert as-is, so a UI that inserts parseMessage as markup gets reflected XSS. The sibling leading-zero path (ipv6.ts:763) does escape the prefix groups, so this path is the exception.
finding.source: Any string passed to `new Address6(str)` or `Address6.isValid`/`fromURL`, for example user input in an address-inspector UI. It only needs characters outside [0-9a-f:/%], for example ``.
finding.sink: `AddressError.parseMessage` (an HTML fragment) at src/ipv6.ts:808, which the consumer inserts via innerHTML. The sink is `address.replace(RE_BAD_CHARACTERS, '$1')`.

trace.note: The constructor takes an attacker-controlled string.
this.parse(addressMinusSuffix) is called after the subnet and zone are stripped. The zone regex `%.*$` removes everything after `%`, but `<`, `>`, quotes and spaces before any `%` remain.
parse4in6 returns the address unchanged unless it has a valid dotted-quad tail. A string like `` has no valid tail (and contains no `:`), so it is returned raw.
RE_BAD_CHARACTERS (`[^0-9a-f:/%]`, v6/constants.ts:61) matches the attacker's `<`, `>`, `=`, quotes and spaces.
An AddressError is thrown with parseMessage = the raw address, with each bad character wrapped in a span and no escapeHtml. The `$1` replacement inserts the bad characters raw.
The doc comment claims the content is HTML-escaped and safe to insert as-is, so consumers will trust it.

finding.guards_checked: helpers.escapeHtml exists (v6/helpers.ts:1) and is used in parse4in6 (ipv6.ts:763), link() (ipv6.ts:1493-1499) and the spanAll helpers, but it is not applied on the bad-character path at ipv6.ts:808. The earlier checks do not constrain the string: RE_SUBNET_STRING and RE_ZONE_STRING only strip a trailing `/N` or `%...`, and the `/` check at ipv6.ts:143 only rejects a stray `/`. The RE_BAD_ADDRESS path at ipv6.ts:817 runs only after the bad-character check passes, so it only sees [0-9a-f:/%] and is safe. Address4 has no parseMessage.
